name: Los Angeles
intro: Los Angeles’s stars come from the MICHELIN Guide California, which has covered the city since 2019. This page includes the starred restaurants in neighbouring Santa Monica, Beverly Hills, West Hollywood, Culver City, Encino and Long Beach. Prices are in US dollars, per person before tax and tip (or the service charge some restaurants add), checked October 2026.
introZh: 也包括鄰近的聖塔莫尼卡、比佛利山莊、西好萊塢、卡爾弗城與長灘的星級餐廳。

localNote.q: How do you book a Michelin star restaurant in LA?
localNote.a: OpenTable is the most used, by {r:melisse} and {r:citrin} (only there since 2024), {r:kato}, {r:orsa-winston} and others. The sushi and omakase counters mostly sell their seats on Tock, among them {r:n-naka} and {r:mori-nozomi}, while {r:providence} still takes bookings by phone as well.

localNote.q: When do tables open at LA’s starred restaurants?
localNote.a: It varies more than elsewhere. Mélisse releases each month in the first week of the month before, {r:somni} a month ahead, {r:lielle} 60 days ahead at 10am every day, and Orsa & Winston up to three months ahead. n/naka opens one week at a time, every Sunday at 10am, a month ahead.

localNote.q: What should you wear to a Michelin star restaurant in LA?
localNote.a: LA is relaxed: Somni suggests business casual, and {r:seline} asks only that you come comfortably dressed. Smart casual fits everywhere.

localNote.q: How much should you tip in LA?
localNote.a: Most of LA’s starred restaurants leave the tip to you. Somni and Orsa & Winston add no service charge, so tip 18–22% of the bill before tax. Sales tax is close to 10% across most of the city.
